To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of AGT, EGFG, and TGFβ-1 mRNA in urine cells may be useful as a non-invasive marker of kidney allograft function.
the expression of AGT, EGFG, and TGF-beta 1 in urine cells may reflect the function of the transplanted kidney and may be useful for the diagnosis of chronic kidney transplant rejection.
Ur mRNA levels of AGAT, EGFR, TGF-1, and TSP-1 may serve as biomarkers for predicting allograft function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of non-invasive biomarkers in Ur of KTRs, which could be useful for predicting allograft function and rejection.
identifying a panel of mRNAs that could be used as non-invasive biomarkers for the diagnosis of CAN.
the evaluation of gene panel mRNAs in urine samples of kidney transplant recipients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of the genes studied here is altered during the first 6 months of KT, and that the expression of some of the genes studied is altered in KTP with more that 6 months post-KT.
the mRNA levels of AG, TGF- β1, EGFR and TSP-1 in Ur samples might reflect the status of allograft.
the mRNA levels of the genes studied in Ur cells are associated with allograft function, but the clinical value of these findings needs to be further evaluated in larger studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of the mRNA of the genes evaluated in the Ur samples of KTP may be a potential marker to predict allograft function.
we have identified a panel of genes that may be useful in predicting the development of CAN.
the mRNA levels of AGTR, EGFR, TSP- 1, and TGFβ1 in Ur cells may be useful non-invasive tools to monitor allograft function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ur mRNA levels of AGTR1, EGFR and TGF- β1 might serve as non-invasive biomarkers of allograft rejection in kidney transplant recipients.
the mRNA levels of Ur cells might reflect the function of the kidney allograft.
